transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I just feel really restless all the time, especially when I’m supposed to sit still in the radiology suite or in class. It’s like I’m crawling out of my skin. I try to tough it out, but I still end up pacing, shifting around, or finding some excuse to get up and move. It’s been going on for months, and it’s getting hard to deal with.
Do you also find yourself feeling anxious, worried, or on edge most of the time, even when there’s no clear reason for it?
Not really. I mean, I get stressed like anyone else, but I wouldn’t say I’m worried or anxious most of the time for no reason. That’s not really what I’m noticing.
Do you find yourself doing certain things over and over again, like checking, counting, or performing rituals, even if you don’t really want to?
No, I don’t think so. I’m not really doing rituals or checking things over and over like that. That doesn’t sound like me.
Have you ever had episodes where you lose awareness, shake, or have uncontrolled movements that might look like seizures, especially in response to stress?
No, I haven’t had anything like that. I don’t lose awareness or shake uncontrollably. Nothing that would look like a seizure, as far as I know.
Do you often feel restless or have trouble staying still in situations where most people wouldn’t have a problem, like sitting through a meeting or watching a movie?

Yeah, definitely. That’s actually a big reason I came in. When I’m supposed to sit still in the radiology suite or in class, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ll keep shifting around, pacing if I can, or I’ll find some excuse to get up and move. I’ve tried to just tough it out for months, but it keeps happening.
When you feel that restlessness or discomfort, do you ever notice physical symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or trembling, especially in stressful situations?
Not really. I mean, I feel uncomfortable and keyed up, but I don’t think of it as my heart racing or sweating or trembling. It’s more just this need to move.
When you feel restless and need to move, do you also feel an inner sense of tension or discomfort that you can't quite explain or relieve?

Yeah, I think so. It’s not like pain or anything, but it’s this uncomfortable, tense feeling, like I’m crawling out of my skin when I’m supposed to sit still. In the radiology suite or in class, I try to tough it out, but after a while I’m shifting around, pacing if I can, or looking for some reason to get up and move.
Do you feel this same restlessness and need to move even when you're not in the radiology suite or in class, like when you're at home watching TV or trying to relax?

Yeah, it happens outside of class too, but it’s most obvious when I’m expected to sit still somewhere. Like in the radiology suite or classroom, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I’ll try to push through it, but I usually end up shifting around, pacing if I can, or finding some reason to get up and move.
Do you find yourself making repetitive movements, like tapping your fingers, shaking your leg, or rocking back and forth, especially when you're feeling restless?

Yeah, I do move around a lot. I’m not sure it’s always one specific thing like rocking, but when I’m supposed to sit still, I feel like I’m crawling out of my skin. I end up shifting in my seat, getting up to pace if I can, or finding some excuse to move around. It’s been going on for months even though I try to just tough it out.

Have you ever experienced times when your thoughts felt disorganized, or when you behaved in ways that others might find strange or unusual, like talking to yourself or reacting to things that aren’t there?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I might talk to myself here and there like thinking out loud, but not like I’m reacting to something that isn’t there. I haven’t noticed my thoughts feeling disorganized in that way or people saying I’m acting strange like that.
Do you often feel impatient or have trouble waiting your turn, like you can't sit still because you want to jump in or get things done right away?

Yeah, definitely. Waiting my turn is really hard for me, especially in lab practice or if I’m waiting for a machine to open up. I get really edgy, like I need to move or do something right then. I’ll keep stepping forward, checking the time, asking if I can go next… and I’ve been called out for it more than once.
Do you often find it hard to focus on tasks, like losing track of what you're doing, getting distracted easily, or not being able to finish things?
I’m not really sure. I do get distracted sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s more than normal. I haven’t really paid attention to whether I’m losing track or not finishing things a lot.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks, like following instructions, keeping your attention on what you're doing, or remembering what you need to do next?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I can usually follow along if it’s clear, but I haven’t paid close attention to whether I’m forgetting steps or losing focus a lot. It might happen sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s a real pattern.
Do you find it difficult to stay focused on tasks, like following instructions, keeping your attention on what you're doing, or remembering what you need to do next, even when the task is important?

I’m honestly not sure. Even if something is important, I haven’t really tracked whether I lose focus or forget what comes next. I can usually do it if I know what I’m supposed to do, but I don’t know if there’s a pattern beyond that.
Do you often find yourself losing focus during tasks, not listening when someone is talking to you directly, or failing to finish things you start, even when you intend to complete them?

I don’t really know. I can think of times where I zone out or don’t catch everything someone says, but I haven’t paid enough attention to say it happens often or that I’m not finishing things because of it.
Do you often find yourself starting tasks but having trouble finishing them, even if they’re important or you meant to complete them?
I’m not really sure. I know I start things and sometimes they take longer than I expected, but I can’t say for sure that I often don’t finish them. I haven’t really noticed a clear pattern with that.
Do you feel this inner sense of restlessness or discomfort even when you're not in situations where you have to sit still, like when you're relaxing at home or doing something you enjoy?

Yeah, I do. Even at home or doing stuff I actually like, like editing photos or sketching, I can’t really stay quiet or settled for long. I’ll start tapping, humming, talking to whoever’s around, or getting up a bunch. People at home or in the lab will tell me to settle down.
